strands.strand: Foundations of Creative Arts and Sports
strands.subStrand: . Careers in Creative Arts and Sports  ● Careers in Creative Arts
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify careers in Creative Arts and Sports, b) illustrate entrepreneurial opportunities in Creative Arts and Sports, c) appreciate careers in Creative Arts and Sports.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  research, using digital devices or print material, to identify and discuss careers in Creative Arts and Sports,  interact with actual or virtual Creative Arts spaces (theatre, recording studio, festivals, galleries, fine arts studios, workshops, exhibitions, cultural and sports centres) to observe roles performed by the personnel,  watch videos/recording of entrepreneurial opportunities in Creative Arts and Sports,  discuss to identify different entrepreneurial opportunities in Creative Arts and Sports,  acknowledge own and others’ talents and areas of career interest in Creative Arts and Sports.
strands.inquiryQuestions: What are the career opportunities related to Creative Arts and Sports?

strands.strand: Foundations of Creative Arts and Sports
strands.subStrand: Components of Creative Arts and Sports   Components of physical fitness - power and reaction time  elements of a play: theme, characters, plot, conflict, resolution, setting, language),  Rhythm: dotted minim, the dotted crotchet and quaver and their rests, ● Note extension: dots and ties
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand the learner should be able to: a) describe the elements of a play, b) perform activities demonstrating the components of fitness, c) name pitches on the grand stave, d) group music notes 4 in time 4 incorporating note extension, e) construct the scale of F major on a staff, f) appreciate the basic elements of Creative Arts and sports.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  watch actual or virtual play performance to identify the elements of a play,  discuss the basic elements of a play  observe actual or virtual activities of fitness that show power and reaction time in physical fitness,  demonstrate fitness exercises that enhance power and reaction time,  practise activities that enhance power and reaction time using music,  draw the grand stave and name lines and spaces,  draw the piano keyboard and relate to the grand stave,  construct the scale of F major on both treble and bass staff,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How does one create harmony pictorial composition? 2. Why should athletes avoid performance enhancers to develop physical fitness? 3. Why is note extension important in music notation?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Drawing and Painting   Drawing  Painting; colour harmony, colour mood(cool/warm ), texture of forms (dabbing))
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) discuss harmony/unity in a picture, b) classify analogous colours on a colour wheel for painting, c) illustrate a colour gradation strip for colour harmony, d) paint a scenery composition to express harmony/unity, e) appreciate own and others pictures,
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● observe pictures to review texture and colour; and discuss unity/harmony, ● paint a colour wheel to classify analogous colours, ● paint line strip using a pair of analogous colours to study colour harmony, ● research to sketch a composition inspired by the surrounding; a sea scape or landscape, ● paint a thin wash using the brush stroke technique to create a background, ● paint the scenery composition to express texture and colour harmony/unity, ● collaboratively, display scenery composition in a
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is colour classification important in painting? 2. How does the colour affect the mood?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Rhythm  Note values: dotted minim, dotted crotchet quaver and their rests
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the effect of note extension on rhythmic patterns, b) compose a four-bar 4 rhythmic pattern in 4 time, c) notate four-bar 4 rhythms in time from 4 dictation, d) appreciate rhythmic patterns as a means of creating interest in Creative Arts and Sports.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  listen to, sing or play tunes involving dotted notes to outline effects of note extension in rhythmic patterns, 4  beat time to familiar tunes in 4 time considering the crochet as principle beat, accented and weak beats,  group notes of given two-bar rhythmic patterns involving 4 dotted notes in time, 4  orally compose 4-bar rhythmic patterns involving dotted notes and their corresponding rests, in 4 time and write on monotone, 4  write rhythmic patterns from dictation,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can various note combinations be used to form rhythms in simple time? 2. How can one improvise accompaniment patterns for Sports?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Athletics and Mosaic   Triple Jump  Long distance running  Mosaic
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to; a) describe the phases in Triple jump, b) perform Triple jump for skill acquisition, c) identify long distance races in athletics, d) perform techniques for long distance running, e) explore characteristics of mosaic in sample pictures, f) create a mosaic pictorial composition inspired by an athletic event, g) acknowledge own and others’ efforts in performing Triple jump, skills in long
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  observe a live or virtual performance of Triple jump to identify the phases,  demonstrate the approach, take off, flight and landing phases in Triple jump,  practise triple jump skills in athletics,  practise technique used in long distance running while observing safety,  observe others’ performance in Triple jump and long distance running skills and give feedback.  collaboratively, play games or engage in athletic events where the skills and techniques in Triple jump and long distance running,  source for actual and virtual samples of mosaic work to
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How has long distance running benefitted Kenya? 2. Why is it important to follow the phases of jumping in triple jump? 3. How can mosaic pictorial composition be used to improve the environment?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Melody   Variations: - rhythmic, melodic, and dynamic variations  Note value involving the dotted minim, dotted crotchet and a quaver,
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the use of variation in composing a melody, b) compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 time, 4 c) notate four-bar, 4 melodies in time, 4 d) perform melodies in F 4 major and time, 4 e) value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  sing familiar tunes and discuss how variation has been achieved in the different phrases of the melody,  perform the scale of F major and its tonic arpeggio,  write a 2-bar answering phrase in F major which is a variation of the given 4 opening phrase in time, 4  improvise 2-bar opening phrases with variation in pitches to given answering 4 phrases in time and F major, 4  create a four-bar melody in F major and 4 in time with varied phrases observing 4 integrity,  add phrase marks to the four-bar composed melodies indicating dynamics as loud for one phrase and soft for the other,
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can a melody be made interesting?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Rugby   Passes: spin, pop and basic  Kicks; place and drop
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learners should be able to: a) distinguish passes in Rugby, b) perform passing skills in Rugby, c) perform kick techniques in Rugby, d) value own and others' efforts in applying passing and kicking skills for enjoyment.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  watch a live, or virtual Rugby game to identify passes and kicks  demonstrate passing skills in Rugby,  practise the spin, pop and basic passes in Rugby,  demonstrate kicking skills in Rugby,  practise the drop and place kick techniques in Rugby,  use the skills of passing and kicking to play a modified game in Rugby while observing the rules of the game and safety.
strands.inquiryQuestions: What are the best ways to advance a ball in a game of Rugby?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Photography   Photography  scenic points (geographical features, building among others)  view point (normal, birds and worm)  presentation; arrangement of photographs, caption,
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learners should be able to: a) identify different viewpoints in photography, b) take photographs of a scenery in viewpoint for showcase, c) present the photographs for appreciation.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● observe virtual and actual samples of photographs to analyse the bird’s, normal and worm’s viewpoints, ● research/take a field walk to explore and identify scenic point in the surroundings, ● take photographs inspired by the environment to showcase beautiful scenes in our country (Kenya) focusing on; varied scene and viewpoints, ● select and store the photographs in an e folder to make a still/slide presentation, ● make a presentation for own reflection and peer feedback in a just manner.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Which are the ethical issues to consider in photography?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Descant Recorder   Technique of pinching  Dynamics: crescendo and diminuendo.
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify the fingering of notes in the scale of F major, b) play the scale of F major from staff notation on a descant recorder, c) perform a solo piece in F major on a descant recorder, applying correct playing techniques, d) value playing music on the descant recorder. .
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  read, and interpret fingering charts to play the notes of F major scale,  play the scale of F Major ascending and descending on staff notation,  play simple melodies in the scale of F major on staff notation,  watch actual or virtual instrumental tutorials to demonstrate and explain techniques of pinching on a descant recorder,  explore actual or virtual demonstrations of playing techniques of descant recorder to explain performance directions for dynamics crescendo and diminuendo, 4  play simple melodies in time, and in 4 F major observing performance directions for dynamics,  use digital devices responsibly to record performances for future reference.
strands.inquiryQuestions: What is the importance of applying technique when playing instrumental music?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Play  ● format of a script- title, playwright, characters, acts, scenes, setting, stage directions and dialogue ● play elements- theme, characters, plot, setting, conflict, language ● Performing a play
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the format of a play script, b) create a one act play addressing a societal issue, c) act a role in a play performance, d) recognise play performance as a channel of addressing societal issues.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● read a sample play to identify the format of a script, ● brainstorm, in groups, an idea for a short play, ● create a short play script using the play elements ● select relevant prop(s), costumes and music for the play performance, ● perform vocal and physical warm up activities in preparation for play performance, ● rehearse a role in the play (paying attention to use of voice, body, movement, space, use of props, music, and costume) ● perform a role in a play performance before an audience, ● record experiences in a journal.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can a play performance be made believable to an audience? 2. Why is it important to decorate props to be used for performance?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Basketball and Logo Design   Passing- overhead, bounce and chest  Dribbling- high and low  Logo design
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) perform passes in Basketball for skill acquisition, b) execute dribbling in Basketball for skill acquisition, c) design logo for a Basketball team, d) appreciate each other’s skills in Basketball game
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● watch a live or virtual Basketball game and identify the passing and dribbling skills in Basketball, ● demonstrate the overhead, bounce and chest passes in Basketball, ● demonstrate high and low dribbling in Basketball, ● practise passing and dribbling skills while observing safety, ● research to examine actual or virtual samples of a logo, ● design a logo for a basketball team, name/letter combination, ● apply the skills learnt in Basketball in a mini-Basketball game in teams displaying the team logos, ● display the logo around the basketball pitch for appreciation.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can a poster be made an effective means of communicating? 2. Why is it important to combine passing and dribbling in Basketball?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Indigenous Kenyan Crafts   pottery  weaving
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe coil techniques in pottery, b) model a vessel using coil method, c) make a frame loom for weaving, d) make a fabric using 2/1 twill weaving technique, e) display and critique own and others’ woven articles.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● study pottery items from actual and virtual sources and analyse coil technique, ● source clay and prepare clay by removing impurities, drying, kneading and wedging, ● make coils of uniform thickness, ● join clay coils to form a vessel, ● smoothen the inside and outside of the vessel, ● decorate the slightly dry vessel by incising and dry under shade. ● collaboratively fire the completely dry vessel using an open pit kiln, ● explore actual and virtual resources to study making a frame loom and 2/1 twill weaves, ● collaboratively, make a wooden mitre joint frame loom, (equal spacing of nails).
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is clay the preferred material for pottery? 2. How is a fabric woven?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Swimming  (Optional)  Standing dive  Butterfly stroke
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe the body position in standing dive and butterfly stroke in swimming, b) perform a standing dive in swimming c) perform the butterfly stroke in swimming, d) appreciate swimming as a life skill.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● watch a live or virtual demonstration to identify the standing dive and butterfly stroke, ● demonstrate the phases of standing dive, ● practise standing dive while observing safety, ● demonstrate the phases of butterfly stroke, ● practise the butterfly stroke while observing safety and coordination,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can swimming skills be performed safely? 2. Why is synchrony important in butterfly stroke?

strands.strand: Creating and Performing
strands.subStrand: Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) Board games
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify types of indigenous board games played in Kenya, b) perform different indigenous board games, c) perform indigenous board games to background music for enjoyment d) appreciate the role played by indigenous board games for mental health.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to: ● watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous board games and identify the skills observed in the games, ● demonstrate indigenous board game skills while observing safety, ● practice skills in different indigenous board games while observing safety ● play games using different indigenous board games with background musical rhythm.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How do indigenous board games enhance mental relaxation? 2. Why are board games considered an indigenous game?

strands.strand: Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports
strands.subStrand: Analysis of Creative Arts and Sports   Analyse Key: C major, G major, F major  Anti-doping in sports  Time signature, 2, 3 , 4 4 4 4  Performance directions- repeat and dynamics  Art catalogue; (name of gallery, artist’s name, type of artwork, medium,
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) analyse a play performance, b) examine ethical practices in sports, c) analyse a solo vocal piece of music, d) critique exhibited artworks for inspiration, e) appreciate the role of analysis in adding value to Creative Arts and Sports.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided to:  research on the criteria for evaluating a play,  analyse a given play performance to evaluate theme, setting, conflict, resolution, use of voice, use of body movement, internalisation, audience involvement, props, costume, overall impression,  discuss ethical issues in Sports (Anti-doping)  research on how to analyse a solo vocal piece of music,  listen to and analyse a solo vocal piece of music,  visit community/online galleries/to see and analyse artworks  create a catalogue of the exhibited artworks,  discuss to reflect on the work of art for inspiration and mentorship,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is analysis an important skill in Creative Arts and Sports? 2. How can analysis of creative arts and sports enhance creativity?
